regime_context: Canada/TSX detector shows Big Banks leading with moderate durability (0.69) and full breadth but crowded; Base Metals rank #2 with zero breadth and low durability, posing no confirmed rotation. Absolute trend gate is active (gate_helps true), historically aiding drawdown control. Rotation is broad (69% eligible) but no single narrative dominates. Macro backdrop is dominated by AI-tech and geopolitics headlines with high unscheduled news share, driving commodity sensitivity.
emerging_watch: Base Metals & Copper: Watch for breadth expansion >0.5 and durability >0.5 as a potential handoff confirmation. Kill if margin vs Banks widens to >1.0 or durability stays sub-0.5 for 15 days.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks exhibit strongest thematic leadership with full breadth, moderate durability, and eligibility under the absolute trend gate, which has validated drawdown control. Crowding (z=1.05) caps size but does not suggest fading; the gate's risk-management edge supports a disciplined overweight.
theses.dissent: Full breadth can signal late-cycle concentration; a credit shock or rapid rate move could reverse banks sharply, and crowded posture heightens unwind risk.

falsifier.text: If ZEB.TO closes below its 50-day moving average and Big Banks durability falls below 0.5 within 30 days, overweight is invalidated.

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals rank #2 but have zero breadth (single-stock concentration) and low durability (0.43). Despite challenger status, the theme lacks real rotation confirmation. Avoid until breadth expands and durability improves.
theses.dissent: A supply shock could rapidly lift copper and broaden participation, making an avoid stance late and costly.

falsifier.text: If XBM.TO breadth rises above 0.5 and durability crosses 0.6 within 20 days, the avoid thesis is proven wrong.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas Producers are eligible but tagged mean-reverting, suggesting trend fragility, and crowded (z=1.03). With macro headlines heavy on geopolitics and unscheduled events, oil prices may whipsaw, making mean-reversion drawdowns a risk. An underweight vs. more stable themes aligns with the gate's risk-control edge.
theses.dissent: A geopolitical supply disruption could spike oil, and energy stocks would rally sharply; underweight would miss that move.

falsifier.text: If WTI crude stabilizes above CAD $85 and XEG.TO outperforms ZEB.TO by 5% over 30 days, underweight is incorrect.

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
